text: canvas_glyphs ( native : Any = None , * , deadline : float | None = None ) -> frozenset [ tuple [ int , str ]] | None Return the glyphs that the active Glyph window shows, or None . None : no Glyph window is the active canvas, so FontLab records package history. Otherwise return one (package id, glyph name) pair for each glyph in the text blocks of the active canvas. Use the name, not the id: CurrentGlyph().id and the canvas slot id of the same glyph differ on 9790 (412 against 531175085312). These are the glyphs that FontLab's canvas history attaches an Undo step to ( flhistorycontroller.cpp , the in_glyphs branch; FontLab issue 8573). Empty slots are skipped. deadline is a time.monotonic() instant (default: now plus CANVAS_SCAN_SECONDS ); a later checkpoint raises TimeoutError . Native read errors propagate. A fontlab module without flWorkspace , or a workspace without getActiveCanvas (offline doubles), has no canvas: return None . FontLab's own module always defines both.
title: fontlabapp.core.edit_guards.canvas_glyphs

text: require_history_scope ( glyphs : Sequence [ Any ], * , creates : bool = False , native : Any = None ) -> None Refuse a write that FontLab would undo only in part (FontLab issue 8573). While a Glyph window is the active canvas, FontLab attaches the Undo step of notifyChangesApplied only to the glyphs that this canvas shows. Other notified glyphs keep the change after Undo (measured on 9790). With the Font window active, the Undo step covers every notified glyph. glyphs : the owner glyphs of the write, matched by font and glyph name. creates : the write makes new glyphs (a new glyph is never in the canvas). Raise ValueError(CANVAS_TEXT) before any write when a Glyph window is the active canvas and the write creates glyphs, or when an owner is not in the canvas. When the canvas cannot be read, use the safe rule: allow no owner, or one owner that is the current glyph, and no new glyph. With no active canvas, return. Call it on the GUI thread only; other threads are refused. native is the fontlab module (default: the native one).
title: fontlabapp.core.edit_guards.require_history_scope

text: require_no_editors ( * , qt : Any = None , deadline : float | None = None ) -> None Refuse a write while any Glyph editor is open, also an inactive one. qt is the PythonQt module (default: the native one). deadline is a time.monotonic() instant (default: now plus EDITOR_SCAN_SECONDS ). Raise ValueError for an open or unreadable editor and TimeoutError when the widget scan passes the deadline. The scan reads only the inherits("GlyphWindow") predicate, with cyclic GC off.
title: fontlabapp.core.edit_guards.require_no_editors

text: require_selection_window ( package_id : int ) -> None Refuse a write unless a Font window of the bound font is active. package_id is the flPackage.id that the caller scanned. Raise ValueError("Activate the Font window before selecting glyphs.") when the active panel is no regular Font window or the font changed. Use it before Unicode writes and before FL.fl.Select / Unselect .
title: fontlabapp.core.edit_guards.require_selection_window

text: require_settled ( native : Any = None ) -> None Refuse a write while FontLab has queued native glyph updates. native is the fontlab module (default: the native one). Read flGlyph.updatedFgGlyphs() once and never clear it: clearing the queue hides the defect instead of avoiding it (FontLab issue 8537).
title: fontlabapp.core.edit_guards.require_settled

text: One native Undo step for a script edit, with auto-layer refusals. What: commit runs a script's font change as ONE FontLab Undo step, in the order that the reviewed App writers use: Refuse before any write ( ValueError , nothing touched): queued native glyph updates only with settled=True (FontLab issue 8537; otherwise disclose them); optionally a missing Font window or an open Glyph editor (Unicode writers); a Glyph window as the active canvas when an owner glyph is not in that canvas (FontLab issue 8573: the Undo step would cover only the shown glyphs; see edit_guards.require_history_scope ); an auto layer in the edit list or among the retained objects; a glyph that the operation policy refuses. checkInitHistoryState(0) on every layer, then every glyph. mutate() . It may return the new native objects it made (for example new layers); they join the notification after the declared layers. One shared UTC lastModified stamp on every glyph. ONE notifyChangesApplied(title, layers + created + glyphs) . With retained objects: ONE notifyChangesApplied(title, retain + layers + created + glyphs, True) . The same stamp again: window observers re-stamp after the history capture. read_back() : the caller compares the font with its plan. Retained objects ( retain= ): a script that removes a component gives the ORIGINAL shape, its shapeData and the builder, read BEFORE the removal ( component_history(shape) ). They go first in the notification, before the layers, and the third argument True asks for deep history. Glyport does the same ( fontlab_backend._retain_component_history and _notify ): its docstring says FontLab 9784 needs this to restore a removed component on Undo (fl#7641). Without retain the call is the two-argument call, unchanged. Steps 4 to 6 run also after a failed mutate , so a partial edit stays on the Undo stack. Every failure is collected and raised as PartialWriteError (a RuntimeError ) whose text says "Native changes may remain; use Edit > Undo". No rollback is tried: Edit > Undo is the recovery. Why the refusals: notifying a list that holds an auto layer makes FontLab re-resolve every default-recipe auto layer in the font, and a change to a base glyph rebuilds its auto composites. Anchors and locks can change and Undo does not restore them (measured; see the workspace AGENTS.md). The policy depends on the operation: "rename" , "unicode" , "geometry" : refuse glyphs that own an auto layer and glyphs that are a base of an auto composite (also through a chain of manual composites). allow_bases=True lets a base through after the user agreed to the rebuild; an auto owner is never let through. "metadata" (notes, tags, mark colours): refuse only glyphs that own an auto layer. How to use:: import fly.ap.core.history.glyphs as history facts = history.scan_auto_facts(package) result = history.commit( "Round Advances", layers, glyphs, lambda: edit(layers), operation="geometry", facts=facts, read_back=check, ) report(result.mismatches) The module imports only the standard library at load time; FontLab modules and fontlabapp.guides.inspect.model load when a function runs. Offline tests prove the call order only, not native Undo/Redo/reopen behaviour.

text: One native Undo step for font-level edits on one or more masters. What: commit_masters writes master values (zones, vertical metrics) as ONE FontLab Undo step. It uses route A of the issue 122 M2 measurement (FontLab 9.0.9790): the history objects of Font Info and "Sync font metrics" ( dlgfontinfo.cpp:2100-2175 , mainwindow_edit.cpp:1208-1226 ): Refuse before any native write ( ValueError ): a thread other than the GUI thread; no active Font window of this font, or a Glyph window as the active canvas (measured in the Font window only); an unknown, duplicate or empty master list; an empty title. Read the queued glyph ids once ( edit_guards.pending_updates ). Never clear them. checkInitHistoryState(0) on the package and on ONE package.mastersContainer() handle. For each requested master, in font order: setMaster(name, False) , read() and save() (the values to restore), write() , read() again and verify() that value. setMaster(original, False) . ONE flItems().notifyChangesApplied(title, [package, container], False) . No glyph and no layer is in the list, so no auto layer is notified. Rollback policy (a decision that differs from history.commit ): history.commit always notifies, also after a failure, and Edit > Undo is the recovery. Here a failure in steps 3 to 5 (a write callback error, or a read-back mismatch) comes BEFORE the notification. So the helper restores every master that it touched, in reverse order, reads each one back, and notifies nothing. Edit > Undo would revert the user's previous step, so no error text recommends it. An interrupt ( KeyboardInterrupt , SystemExit ) also runs the rollback and the master restore, then is raised unchanged. All values restored: raise RolledBackError (a ValueError : the font is as before, like a refusal). A caller whose restore re-creates native objects passes restored_text to say so ( zone_native ). A restore failed, or the notification failed: raise UnrestoredError (a history.PartialWriteError ). Values can remain with no Undo step. Known host defect (fl#8574, measured on 9.0.9790, issue 122 M2): after Edit > Undo or Redo of such a step, both masters show only 3 of the 9 font-metric guidelines (the zone guidelines) until package.updateFontMetrics() runs or the font is reopened. The saved file is correct. This module does not patch Undo; it cannot hook the user's Undo. How to use:: import fly.ap.core.history.masters as font_history edit = font_history.MasterEdit(save, write, read, verify, restore) result = font_history.commit_masters(package, "Edit Zones", {"Bold": edit}) edit_guards.disclose(result) The module imports only the standard library at load time. Offline tests prove the call order only, not native Undo/Redo/reopen behaviour.

text: auto_facts ( records : Iterable [ Record ]) -> AutoFacts Build AutoFacts from dependency records, one record per layer. Use the records of fontlabapp.guides.inspect.model.dependency_values(package) : (glyph name, layer is auto, component base names) . title: fontlabapp.core.history.glyphs.auto_facts

text: commit ( title : str , layers : Sequence [ Any ], glyphs : Sequence [ Any ], mutate : Callable [[], Iterable [ Any ] | None ], * , operation : Operation , facts : AutoFacts , allow_bases : bool = False , read_back : Callable [[], Iterable [ str ]] | None = None , settled : bool = False , window : int | None = None , native : Any = None , stamp : Any = None , retain : Sequence [ Any ] = (), glyph_window_ok : bool = False ) -> Committed Run mutate as ONE native Undo step. See the module text for the order. title : the Undo name. layers : every existing layer that mutate changes (all layers of a glyph for renames and Unicode). glyphs : their owner glyphs. mutate() : the edit; return new native objects to notify, or None . operation and facts : the refusal policy ( facts from a fresh scan_auto_facts ). allow_bases : let bases of auto composites through after the user agreed. read_back() : return one text per mismatch between font and plan. settled : refuse queued native updates (explicit opt-in; default False discloses pre-write ids in Committed.pending_updates without clearing them). window : the bound package id; when given, run require_selection_window and require_no_editors first (Unicode writers). native / stamp : the fontlab module and the UTC stamp; the defaults are the native module and QDateTime.currentDateTimeUtc() . retain : native objects to keep in the Undo state, first in the list, with the deep-history flag True (use component_history for each removed component, read before the removal). They get no checkInitHistoryState and are not in Committed.created . Empty: the two-argument notification, as before. glyph_window_ok : skip the Glyph-window check ( edit_guards.require_history_scope ). Use it only for a caller that a native test proves safe; no caller uses it now. Raise ValueError before any history call for a refusal. Raise PartialWriteError when anything fails after history started, including a new auto layer from mutate (it stays out of the notification).
title: fontlabapp.core.history.glyphs.commit

text: component_history ( shape : Any ) -> tuple [ Any , ... ] Return the native objects to retain when a script removes shape . What: (shape, shape.shapeData, shapeData.builder) for a component; () for any other shape, so the result can always go to commit(..., retain=...) . Same logic as glyport's _retain_component_history . When: call it BEFORE removeShape , outside mutate . Glyport records that a builder read after detachment can already be too late (fl#7641). A component without shapeData raises ValueError : nothing to retain is a fault, not an empty result. The builder is returned as FontLab gives it.
title: fontlabapp.core.history.glyphs.component_history

Texts: "has auto layers" for an auto owner (every operation); "base of auto X, Y…" for a base of auto composites ( "rename" , "unicode" , "geometry" , unless allow_bases ). An unknown operation raises ValueError .

text: The callbacks for one master. text: feature_text ( tag : str , pairs : Iterable [ tuple [ str , str ]]) -> str Build a complete substitution block without a trailing newline. Require a four-character ASCII alphanumeric tag, safe glyph names and unique source names. Preserve pair order; empty pairs produce an empty block. The result is source text, not proof that the feature compiles or shapes correctly. Ordered native writers may require a final newline.
title: fontlabapp.features.code.feature_text

text: safe_name ( name : str ) -> bool Return whether a glyph name can appear unescaped in generated FEA. Permit ASCII letters/underscore initially and letters, digits, dots or hyphens thereafter, plus .notdef. This is intentionally conservative: it does not parse escaped FEA names or verify a glyph exists in a font.
title: fontlabapp.features.code.safe_name

text: suffix_pairs ( names : Iterable [ str ], suffix : str ) -> list [ tuple [ str , str ]] Return unique existing base/alternate pairs in alternate-name order. Ignore leading suffix dots, orphan alternates and unsafe names. Every generated pair needs both names in the supplied glyph-name iterable. Empty suffixes yield no pairs. No font or feature source is modified.
title: fontlabapp.features.code.suffix_pairs

text: Explicit sources and destination folder; one run at a time. Start validates every job in FontLab first (Fontport's run() is eager) and writes nothing on failure. The work then runs in a separate Python 3.11+ with fontlab-fontport (python=..., else $FONTLABAPP_BATCH_PYTHON), so it never holds FontLab's GIL; each 50 ms poll reads at most 64 KiB and records at most 64 rows from a non-blocking pipe. Output that is not a result row stops the run visibly. Cancel stops before the next font. Close (including parent or own-widget destruction) cancels and returns at once; batch_worker.supervise then collects the child (terminated after GRACE_SECONDS, killed later; a terminated font can leave a partial destination), removes its scratch files and deletes the hidden, detached panel. Outputs are named -transformed.ufo and never replace a file.

Native object ids guard the UI binding; fgId identifies the fontpr font. Raise ValueError when the bound font is no longer the active font.

text: write_feature_blocks ( package : Any , expected : dict , updated : dict , * , references : Iterable [ str ], undo_name : str ) -> dict [ str , int ] Apply an exact source-bound feature plan with Fontport's history checks. All referenced glyphs and the complete source snapshot must still match. Fontport validates split-back, language synthesis and empty history slots before mutation, and notifies only package/features. Groups are untouched. Unexpected native errors may leave partial changes; they are not hidden. Refuse with ValueError when the font is inactive, the source differs from expected , or a referenced glyph is gone. Return {"changed": 0} when expected == updated and {"changed": 1} after a write. The master that was active before the write is restored in finally .

text: follow_changes ( owner , callback , fonts , delay_ms = CHANGE_DELAY_MS ) Call callback after FontLab reports changes; return signals connected. Connected whenever FontLab is present (nothing outside it); fonts() is read at each signal, so an owner whose fonts appear later starts following then. Signals count only while fonts() holds a FontLab-backed font, and glyph(s)Updated only for those documents. The first signal arms a single-shot timer that later signals never restart, so callback runs at most delay_ms after the first change even under a steady stream. Signals emitted while any follower's callback runs (refresh reads or writes, also from other open controls) are ignored, no callback is re-entered, and a timer that fires during another follower's callback runs after it. Before it, each FontLab-backed (Fontport) font is refreshed, which drops its loaded glyph and layer handles. owner.close() disconnects everything; a pending timer then fires into nothing.
title: fontlabapp.fontui.lifecycle.follow_changes

text: follow_history ( owner , callback ) Call callback after FontLab's Undo/Redo actions; return connections made. FontLab connects its own handlers first, so ours run after the history step. Outside FontLab (no fontlab module) nothing is connected. owner.close() disconnects these like every other owned connection.

text: Shared kernel of the scripts that make new glyphs from copies of existing ones. What: Small Caps From Capitals, Superior & Inferior Figures and Tabular Figure Copies plan one new glyph per selected source glyph and copy its contours, transformed, into every master. This module holds the parts that were byte-identical in the three scripts: survey_with plans one Row per selected name with the script's naming rule. It lists and skips a repeated target, a missing source, a target that exists, a source layer that cannot be copied ( source_problem ) and, without the user's consent, a target that can make FontLab rebuild automatic glyphs ( Row.rebuild ). create makes the planned glyphs through fontlabapp.glyphs.creation.create_glyphs : each glyph with its master widths, then all contours in one Undo step, then a read-back. panel_type() returns CopiesPanel , the shared panel of the three scripts (a fontlabapp.contours.selection.panel.model panel with a source table and the rebuild consent tick). How: a job is (new name, [(master, contours, advance)]) ; the script's prepare builds it with fontlabapp.contours.copy.copy_contours . Undo: glyph_creation.UNDO_TEXT . This module imports only the standard library and stdlib-only App modules at load time; PythonQt loads in panel_type() and fontlab in create . Offline tests do not prove native Undo/Redo. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.glyphs.copies as glyph_copies rows = glyph_copies.survey_with(package, names, naming, facts, allow_rebuild) result = glyph_copies.create(package, jobs, "Small Caps", facts, allow_rebuild=True)

text: Create new glyphs through FontLab's own Add Glyph command, then fill them in one step. What: the Contours creator scripts (Placeholder Glyphs, Small Caps From Capitals, Superior & Inferior Figures, Tabular Figure Copies) make new glyphs. create_glyphs does it in this order: Refuse before any change ( ValueError ): a name listed twice, a name that exists now, a name that can make FontLab rebuild an automatic glyph ( auto_candidates ) without the user's consent, a Glyph window as the active canvas ( edit_guards.require_history_scope , FontLab issue 8573: measured on 9790, Undo stays disabled for the new glyphs and their outlines there). Read queued native glyph updates for disclosure (FontLab issue 8537); never clear them. Read the signature of every automatic layer ( auto_signatures ). For each new glyph, call the fontpr tool set_glyph(create=True) with the name, one layer per master with its advance width, the code points and optional components ( NewGlyph.components , Part ; glyph_data ). The components are checked after the call. FontLab runs its undoable Add Glyph command ( commAddGlyph ) for it. Optionally fill the new layers in ONE history.commit(..., operation="geometry") that declares the new layers and glyphs. Read back: the caller's read_back texts, then one text per automatic layer whose signature changed ( auto_changes ). User text for the Undo shape: UNDO_TEXT ("Each new glyph is recorded as its own Undo step, and the outlines as one more Undo step."). This module makes no claim about what Undo restores. Why: flPackage.addGlyph is a raw insert. It runs no command and records no history (source: flpackage.cpp:18526-18532 ), and it skips ensureComplete . set_glyph creates the glyph the way FontLab's own tools do (source: mcptools_source.cpp:144-172 ); the command runs synchronously and clears the queued glyph updates ( flhistorycontroller.cpp:1818-1914 ). Glyport creates glyphs the same way. This module never calls addGlyph and never writes a FontGate record. The Add Glyph command re-resolves the default-recipe automatic composites of the font ( commAddGlyph::updateAutoGlyphs , fl#8512). FontLab gives no Python call that predicts a default recipe, so auto_candidates is a conservative guess: automatic layers without an own recipe whose glyph name shares a dotted suffix segment with the new name (a new e.sc can change eacute.sc ). The script lists them ("may rebuild auto eacute.sc") and creates such a glyph only after the user ticks REBUILD_LABEL . The after-write check ( auto_changes ) stays. Automatic layers are never notified. This module imports only the standard library and stdlib-only App modules at load time; fontpr loads when create_glyphs runs. Offline tests prove the call order, not native Undo/Redo. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.glyphs.creation as glyph_creation specs = [glyph_creation.NewGlyph("h.sc", (("Regular", 450),))] done = glyph_creation.create_glyphs(package, specs, "Small Caps", facts, fill=fill)

text: capture ( * , deadline : float | None = None ) -> Any Read the glyph names, Unicode values and dates of the current font. What: return an immutable fontlabapp.qt.tables.filter.model.Table with the columns "Glyph name", "Unicode" and "Modified" in font order. rows holds (name, "U+0041 U+00C1", "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss") tuples and epochs holds the modification instants ( None when unset). How: the private _glyph_catalog_native.capture reads the whole font twice from FontGate records mapped by package.findFgId . It never reads flGlyph.fgGlyph . A change between the reads rejects the whole result. Use: call it on the main UI thread. deadline is a time.monotonic() instant; the default budget is two seconds. It raises ValueError with no open font or a changed font, TimeoutError after the deadline and RuntimeError off the main thread. It writes nothing. Native preservation is not proved by offline tests.

text: auto_candidates ( package : Any , facts : AutoFacts , names : Iterable [ str ]) -> dict [ str , tuple [ str , ... ]] Map each new name to the automatic glyphs that FontLab may rebuild when it appears. A candidate owns a layer with autoLayer and no own recipe (a default-recipe automatic layer), and its name shares a whole dotted suffix segment with the new name ( e.sc and eacute.sc ; not x.scale ). A new name without a dot gets no candidates. Names without candidates are left out. Only the owners in facts.autos are read. Scope: this is a pre-write HEURISTIC for the consent tick, not a prediction. Adding ANY glyph re-resolves every automatic layer of the font: Add Glyph passes every glyph id to _process_update_auto_layers ( flhistorycontroller.cpp:1910-1921 ) and UpdatePackageData::updateAutoLayers walks every auto layer ( update_components.cpp:716-790 ). So any new name, dotted or not ( acute and Aacute ), can change any default-recipe automatic glyph. The guard is the after-write auto_changes check. This is a reading of the source, not a measurement.
title: fontlabapp.glyphs.creation.auto_candidates

text: create_glyphs ( package : Any , specs : Sequence [ NewGlyph ], title : str , facts : AutoFacts , * , fill : Callable [[ dict [ str , Any ]], None ] | None = None , read_back : Callable [[], Iterable [ str ]] | None = None , allow_rebuild : bool = False ) -> Created Create every glyph of specs , then optionally fill them in ONE Undo step. facts : a fresh history.scan_auto_facts(package) . fill(glyphs) gets {name: new package glyph} and edits the new master layers (find them with glyph.findLayer(master) ); it runs inside one history.commit(title, layers, glyphs, ..., operation="geometry") that declares every new layer and glyph. read_back() returns one text per mismatch with the plan. allow_rebuild : the user ticked REBUILD_LABEL ; it also goes to the commit as allow_bases . Raise ValueError before any change for a refusal (module text, step 1). When FontLab refuses the FIRST glyph before its command runs, raise RuntimeError ("... did not start ... No glyph was added.") without the Undo hint. Every other failure raises history.PartialWriteError (with history.UNDO_HINT ); after the first glyph exists its text names the new glyphs. Nothing to create returns Created((), ()) with no native call.

text: Whole-font snapshot, refusals and one-Undo commit for the Names editors. What: the Names editors (Batch Rename, Suffix Tool, Unicode From Names, Glyph Notes, Batch Glyph Notes, Glyph Tags, Mark Color Palette) share one model: scan() reads every glyph of the current font into Facts : one Entry per glyph (FontGate record plus FontLab glyph) and the auto-layer facts of the whole font ( history.AutoFacts ). refusal / editable say which glyphs an operation may edit. fresh_facts scans again just before a write, refuses a switched font and leaves pre-write disclosure to commit . commit runs the edit as ONE Undo step through history.commit . How: scan maps each font-owned record through package.findFgId and checks name and id both ways. It never reads flGlyph.fgGlyph : on build 9784 that getter can clear a fresh note mirror. Facts is never patched; a stale snapshot is scanned again. Why the refusals ( history.refusal ): FontLab rebuilds every auto layer when an auto layer or a base of an auto composite is notified, and Undo does not restore the result (after e was renamed, ecircumflex became a lone ee ). Use operation="rename" or "unicode" for names and code points, "metadata" for notes, tags and mark colours (these refuse only glyphs that own an auto layer). How to use:: import fly.ap.glyphs.names.model as names_edit facts = names_edit.fresh_facts(package_id) ok, refused = names_edit.editable(facts, names, "rename") names_edit.commit("Batch Rename", [facts.entries[n] for n in ok], lambda: rename(ok), operation="rename", facts=facts) The module imports only the standard library at load time. Offline tests do not prove native Undo/Redo/reopen behaviour.

text: PostScript hint counts of a layer, by FontLab's hint role. What: hint_counts(layer) returns the (horizontal, vertical) counts of the PostScript stem hints of a layer. Contours > Autohint Selected Layers and Remove PostScript Hints show these counts before and after a write. How: a hint is a guide object with isHint . Its direction is its role, read with the callable isHorizontal() and isVertical() of flGuideLine (the same calls as fontlabapp.metrics.zones.capture ). Why the role and not the angle: flLayer.removeHints(horizontal, vertical) selects hints by the role flag (source: fllayer.cpp:6293-6312 , flsnapline.cpp:4377-4389 ), not by the angle that isVerticalQuarter tests. So these counts agree with what FontLab removes. A hint with neither role is in neither count; FontLab's removeHints removes such a hint in every direction. Plain guidelines are not counted. This module imports nothing at load time beyond typing. Offline tests do not prove native FontLab behaviour. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.hints.postscript as hints horizontal, vertical = hints.hint_counts(layer)

text: Clamp every master's explicit kerning through the qualified batch writer. Independent implementation of Vassil Kateliev/Karandash Type Foundry's Science Gothic Kerning Cutoff Filter v1.1 (2025). text: associated_master ( name : str , masters : Sequence [ str ]) -> str | None Return the master that a layer name belongs to, or None. What: drop a leading |temp| , cut at the first @ (else the first # ) and return the rest when it is one of masters . So "Regular@ 2026-10-21" and "Regular#bracket" belong to "Regular" ; "mask.Regular" and "Light Copy" belong to none. Why: this is FontLab's own rule ( flLayer::isMasterLayerName , fllayer.cpp:10346-10375, which then calls package.hasMaster ). Scripts that step through, copy or promote layers use it to find the master of a backup or a bracket layer. Pure string work; it reads no font.
title: fontlabapp.masters.inspect.model.associated_master

text: backup_layer_name ( base : str , taken : Iterable [ str ], suffix : str , masters : Sequence [ str ]) -> str Return a unique <base> backup <suffix> name, or raise ValueError. Strip the suffix and refuse an empty value. Append (2), (3) and so on for case-insensitive collisions in taken . Refuse @, # or |temp| anywhere in the candidate, a master name (casefold), or a name that does not resolve exactly to base . These checks keep the backup out of special layer roles and prevent a restore to the wrong master. Example: backup_layer_name("Bold", names, "trial", masters) .
title: fontlabapp.masters.inspect.model.backup_layer_name

text: backup_master ( name : str , masters : Sequence [ str ]) -> str | None Return the master of a plain or legacy backup layer, or None. Refuse names equal to any master (casefold), and names with # or |temp| anywhere. For legacy @ names, match the part before @. Otherwise use the longest master plus a space prefix. Prefix matches use exact case, as the layer tools always did: regular sketch is not a backup of Regular, and with masters Bold and BOLD, BOLD backup x belongs to BOLD. With Bold and Bold Italic, Bold Italic backup x belongs to Bold Italic; Bold Italic itself is never a backup. Use this rule for display, cleanup and restore tools.
title: fontlabapp.masters.inspect.model.backup_master
